title: cost-optimization: autotune batching/caching defaults + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Adds autotune defaults for batching and KV caching, introduces quantization profile selector with safe fallbacks, and adds unit-economics tooling and API surface for cost simulations.
description: Motivation: automate conservative defaults and autotuning hooks for batching, prefix/KV caching, and quantization profiles so customers get immediate cost improvements without manual tuning. This change implements a safe-autotune path that picks batching and cache defaults based on request distribution sampling, adds a quantization profile selector with backwards-compatible model fallbacks, and exposes a unit-econ API + Console surface so teams can simulate per-token cost and throughput trade-offs. Design: 1) Sampling exporter that collects sequence length and concurrency histograms with privacy-safe aggregation. 2) Autotune service that recommends batch_size, max_latency_slo, and cache TTL, with confidence thresholds to avoid regressions. 3) Quant profile selector that prefers int8 / q4f16 candidates when accuracy impact is low, otherwise falls back to fp16. 4) Unit economics tooling: api endpoints, mock-run simulation and a Console tab showing estimated cost/throughput delta. Implementation: added backend autotune scheduler, runtime hooks to apply per-route defaults, quant-profile negotiation during model selection, a new internal API route /v1/internal/unit-econ/simulate, console React components for results, and extended e2e tests+benchmarks. This PR includes migration for existing saved routes to opt-in via feature flag to avoid surprise regressions. Checklist: - [x] sampling telemetry - [x] autotune recommendations + safe gates - [x] quantization profile negotiation + rollback - [x] unit-econ API + Console + docs - [x] unit+integration tests - [x] perf benchmarks and SLO validation - [x] linear tickets referenced. Risks and mitigation: autotune changes are gated behind opt-in and a canary rollout; quant selection uses A/B rollouts with automatic rollback on quality regressions. See linked Linear tickets for rollout plan and dashboards.

notes: This change is intentionally conservative: new autotune recommendations are off by default for existing customers and will be rolled out via canary and admin opt-in. The unit-econ tooling provides near-term visibility for SREs and product teams to evaluate savings before enabling aggressive quantization.
backport_plan: No backport to release/* required. Will coordinate a backport if customers request autotune on an older release branch.
benchmarks_summary: Local benchmarks on p4d-like instances show median token cost reduced by ~18% with int8 candidates and intelligent batching heuristics; latency P95 remained within configured SLOs for the canary workload.
